Class SysMLItem

java.lang.Object
sysmlinjava.common.SysMLAnything
sysmlinjava.occurrences.SysMLOccurrence
sysmlinjava.items.SysMLItem
Direct Known Subclasses:
AnimatedAreaDisplayData, SysMLMetadata, SysMLPart, SysMLSignal
public abstract class SysMLItem extends SysMLOccurrence
SysMLinJava's represention of the SysML item.

The item in SysMLinJava

SysMLItem is an abstract class that provides a base class for for all SysML item representations. Extensions of the SysMLItem class declare features (as fields) and owned actions (as methods). Features may include SysML attributes, items, requirerements, and dependencies.

Creating/initializing features

The SysMLItem provides a series of overrideable method calls to create all the features (the Java fields) of the represented SysML item (a Java class). The SysMLItem constructor automatically invokes methods to create/initialize the attributes, items, requirements, and dependencies. This automatice invocation of methods allows extensions to the SysMLItem to simply override the createXxxx() methods for the applicable features (fields) declared in the item (class) and perform the creations/initializations in the create methods. This ensures the features are created/initialized in the correct and complete sequence needed. The overridable createXxxx() methods provide a framework for the features' complete definitions as well as a "reminder" to create and initialize the item's features.

A simplified example of code for an item model follows: 

public class InputPower extends SysMLItem
{
        @Attribute
        public ElectricPotentialVolts voltage;
        @Attribute
        public ElectricCurrentAmps current;

        @Requirement
        public SysMLRequirement standardPowerRequirement;

        public InputPower(ElectricPotentialVolts voltage, ElectricCurrentAmps current, String name, Long id)
        {
                super(name, id);
        }

        @Override
        public void createAttributes()
        {
                voltage = new ElectricPotentialVolts(120);
                current = new ElectricCurrentAmps(15);
        }

        @Override
        protected void createRequirements()
        {
                standardPowerRequirement = SystemRequirements.id3_2_1;
        }
}

      protected void createAttributes()
      Overridable operation that creates and initializes the part's attributes.

      Code format: 

              @Attribute
        LubricantTypeAFlow inlet!Flow;
        @Attribute
        LubricantTypeBFlow inlet2Flow;
        @Attribute
        VolumeMetersCubed size;
        @Attribute
        WeightNewtons weight;
        @Attribute
        PowerWatts powerIn;
        @Attribute
        HeatWatts heatOut;
                :
        protected void createAttributes()
        {
                inlet1Flow = new LubricantTypeAFlow(25);
                inlet2Flow = new LubricantTypeBFlow(2);
                VolumeMetersCubed size = new VolumeMetersCubed(0.588;
                WeightNewtons weight = new WeightNewtons(0.55);
                PowerWatts powerIn = new PowerWatts(65);
                HeatWatts heatOut = new HeatWatts(45);
        }

    • createEvents

      protected void createEvents()
      Overridable operation that creates and initializes the part's declared events.

      Code format:

              @TimeEvent
        SysMLTimeEvent myTimeEvent;
        @CallEvent
        MyCallEvent myCallEvent;

        protected void createEvents()
        {
           myTimeEvent = new SysMLTimeEvent(<initializer>);
           myCallEvent = new MyCallEvent(<initializer>);
        }

      where the the targets of the assignment operations are the names of fields with the &#64;TimeEvent and &#64;CallEvent annotations and new SysMLTimeEvent and MyCallEvent are constructors of a specific time event and an extended/specialized call event, respectively.

      Note this operation is likely seldom used as events are typically instantiated when the event occurs rather than as part of part construction - the exception being the SysMLTimeEvent, which is used to start timers as well as to indicate timer expiration.

      See Also:
      • SysMLEvent
      • SysMLCallEvent
      • SysMLChangeEvent

    • createStateMachine

      protected void createStateMachine()
      Overridable operation that creates/initializes the part's state machine, if any. (The default is for the part to have no state machine.) The stateMachine is declared as a variable of (@code SysMLItem}. This variable should be created/initialized in an override of the createStateMachine() method. An example follows: 
      	public class MyItem extends SysMLItem
	{
			:
		&#64;Override
		protected void createStateMachine()
		{
			stateMachine = Optional.of(new MyItemsStateMachine(this));
		}
			:
	}
      See Also:
      • SysMLStateMachine

    • createConstraintFunctions

      protected void createConstraintFunctions()
      Overridable operation that creates and initializes the constraint function (lambda expressiuns) for the item's constraints. An example is as follows: 
      	{
		&#64;Attribute
		int totalPower;
		&#64;Attribute
		int electricalPower;
		&#64;Attribute
		int mechanicalPower;

		&#64;Attribute
		int totalWeight;
		&#64;Attribute
		int componentWeight;
		&#64;Attribute
		int containerWeight;

		&#64;FunctionalInterface
		public interface NextConstraint extends SysMLAction.ActionBody
		{
			int totalWeight(int waterWeight, int containerWeight);
		}

		&#64;ConstraintFunction
		BasicConstraintFunction totalPowerOKFunction;
		&#64;ConstraintFunction
		NextConstraint totalWeightFunction;

		void createConstraintFunctions()
		{
			totalPowerOKFunction = (BasicConstraintFunction)() -> return totalPower > electricalPower + mechanicalPower);
			totalWeightFunction = (NextConstraint)(componentsWeight, containerWeight) -> { return componentsWeight + containerWeight;});
		}
	}
      See Also:
      • SysMLConstraint

    • createConstraintTexts

      protected void createConstraintTexts()
      Overridable operation that creates and initializes the constraint texts (documentations) for the item's constraints. An example is as follows: 
      	{
		&#64;Attribute
		int totalPower;
		&#64;Attribute

		&#64;Attribute

		&#64;Attribute
		int totalWeight;
		&#64;Attribute
		int componentWeight;
		&#64;Attribute
		int containerWeight;

		&#64;ConstraintText
		SysMLDocumentation totalPowerOKDoc;
		&#64;ConstraintText
		SysMLConstraintText totalWeightDoc;

		void createConstraintTexts()
		{
			totalPowerOKDoc = new SysMLDocumentation("totalPower > electricalPower + mechanicalPower");
			totalWeightDoc = new SysMLDocumentation("totalWeight = componentsWeight + containerWeight");
		}
	}

    • createRequirements

      protected void createRequirements()
      Overridable operation that initializes the item's requirements. An example follows: 
              @SatisfyRequirement
        SysMLRequirement itemsFirstRequirement;
        @SatisfyRequirement
        SysMLRequirement itemsNextRequirement;
                :
        protected void createRequirements()
        {
                itemsFirstRequirement = SystemRequirements.1_3_2_4;
                itemsNextRequirement = SystemRequirements.1_3_2_5;
        }
      Note that item requirements should be declared as described above, i.e. as references to instantiations of SysMLRequirements declared and initialized in classes that extend/specialize the SysMLRequirements class. Requirements should not be defined/specified in the item itself. Requirement specifications are in the form of instances of the SysMLRequirement or specializations/extensions thereof. Specializations/extensions should be declared in a requirements package in the model, as suggested by the SysML standard. Instances of all requirements, be it of basic SysMLRequirements or of extensions/specializations, should be declared as static instances in a class that is an extension of the SysMLRequirements class. Declaring all requirement instances in a single class conforms to the SysML standard of declaring requirement in a single collection/package. It also enables SysMLinJava tools to be used to manage and query the requirements.
      See Also:
      • SysMLRequirement
      • SysMLRequirementsCollection

      protected void createDependencies()

              {
                @Dependency
                SysMLDependency usage;

    • createCustomMetadatas

      protected void createCustomMetadatas()
      Overridable operation that creates and initializes custom item metadata, i.e. metadata that is not one of the standard SysaML metadata types. (Standard metadata elements should be created in overrides of create...() methods in the SysMLAnything class. An example of creating custom metadata instances is as follows: 
              {
                @Metadata
                SWAPMetadata swap;
                        :
                protected void createCustomMetadata()
                {
                        swap = new SWAPMetadata(25, 15, 15);
                }
        }
